summary: This skill wraps the Nansen CLI (`nansen research profiler ...`) to profile and compare blockchain wallets: balance, PnL, labels, transactions, counterparties, related wallets, batch and multi-hop trace. It needs the `nansen` binary, installed from the npm package nansen-cli, and a Nansen API key (NANSEN_API_KEY) or a saved browser login session. Calls can trigger automatic x402 payments from a configured wallet, and each call, including calls in loops, can cost money. Queries go to Nansen's API, which the files do not name directly.

findings.message: metadata.openclaw sets primaryEnv NANSEN_API_KEY while requires.env declares nothing, so the API key the skill relies on is not declared as a required env var.
The instructions say NANSEN_API_KEY overrides the saved session, so this credential is used even though requires.env does not list it.

API keys and browser sessions use automatic x402 payments that can spend funds from the configured wallet on a supported HTTP 402 challenge, so the skill relies on wallet authorization that no metadata declares.
The skill card acknowledges that authenticated research calls may consume credits or trigger x402 wallet payments, and tells the user to review the payment policy and spending limits.
The metadata installs the npm package nansen-cli, which provides the nansen binary; it is third-party code fetched at install time and must be trusted.
allowed-tools grants Bash(nansen:*), letting the agent run any nansen subcommand without a per-command prompt.
The trace command makes N*width paid API calls, and batch and counterparties-batch also multiply calls, so cost can escalate quickly in loops.

Browser login requests the nansen:api scope, which gives API-key-equivalent account permissions, and the Nansen service receives the queried wallet addresses; the files name no host beyond a github.com docs link.
